title: お客さまがきた

plotSummary: A guest arrives at the Moomin house. It is the Hemulen, bumbling, apologetic — he dropped something on the way, he heard something strange in the storm, he intends to come back tomorrow. Moominmamma receives him with complete ます/です politeness. This is the chapter where polite narration becomes formally available: the register that one uses with a feared or unfamiliar guest. The Groke (モラン) is mentioned but does not arrive — she is who the Hemulen thought he saw.

scene.location: ムーミンやしきの玄関
scene.beat: A guest arrives. The Hemulen at the door. Polite ます/です takes its home step — because you meet the feared guest politely.

focusVocab.gloss: intention; V-dict + つもり = plan to V

glossary.gloss: intention; V-dict + つもり = plan to V

grammarNotes: V-ます — the polite-present form. 探します = "[I] search (politely)"; 落としました = "[I] dropped (polite past)." The Hemulen's whole register is polite.
N + です / でした — the polite copula. ここです = "[it] is here"; 大変でした = "[it] was terrible."

すみません — the real apology of polite Japanese, which the Hemulen repeats. (悪い as apology exists — わるいね — but it is CASUAL male register; welded to です it is neither casual nor polite. This chapter models the correct pairing: polite register, polite apology.)
V-dict + つもり — "intend to V." 来るつもりです = "[I] intend to come"; 行くつもりだよ = "[I] mean to go" (casual).

WATCH THE ENDING CHANGE: from p20 to the end, the NARRATOR puts on ます/です to see the guest out — 落としました, 渡しました, すごしました, わかりません. Polite narration is a register the narrator can choose, and it enters exactly here, at the chapter that teaches it. From ch26 the narration returns to plain form; the polite coat hangs by the door.

The register contrast in dialogue: the Hemulen is polite throughout; Mama matches him warmly; Moomintroll stays casual (つもりだよ, 見てみるよ) — a child is not expected to keigo a guest. Register shifts by speaker and listener.
